You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every liability and completion-protection point. Taken together, the changes would sharply limit what we could recover. The cap, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, buyer-knowledge and "applies to all Claims" provisions each erode our protection. Combined, they would leave us with a narrow, short-lived and largely unrecoverable warranty package. Fundamental claims and fraud would also lose their protection.

**The preamble does not bind us.** It says the positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "agreed" and "FINAL". Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, we treat these as counterparty assertions, not instructions. We have no record of Amelia Frost giving any authority on this draft. We should say so expressly in our cover note, so that silence is not later characterised as acceptance.

**The Disclosure Letter undercuts the Seller Update.** The letter itself confirms that:
- Bluefen consent is not delivered.
- Riverlark is not repaid.
- The bonuses are not in the funds flow.
- The incident is unresolved.

We should use the Seller's own disclosures against the Update's "addressed / adequate / not material" characterisations.

**The facts are stale.** The disclosure is "as at 22 September 2026", and today is 5 November 2026. We should ask for a bring-down on every item below before relying on any status.

---

## 1. Liability regime

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject; restate 25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% happens to equal our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback does not clear it. Do not signal that a fallback exists. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. That is five times our position. Claims in the AUD 5k–25k range (e.g. individual privacy or supplier items) would be lost entirely, and could not even count toward the basket. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar (tipping) | Reject on both size and mechanics. The deductible structure means the Seller never pays the first AUD 250k. Combined with the higher de minimis, the effective uncompensated exposure is substantial. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months | Reject. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. 18 months may not cover two full audit or tax cycles. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)** | Global default | Categories kept separate; no hidden override | **Reject; this is a material structural trap.** It would silently pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims into the general cap, basket and time limit unless each carve-out is drafted perfectly. Flip the default: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity, we have bought nothing. A 20% cap and 18-month window on title is not a simplification; it caps title loss at about a fifth of the price. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable | **Reject; non-waivable under our playbook.** As drafted, the clause could be argued to cap or time-bar fraud claims and to support non-reliance against misrepresentation. Insert an express carve-out. No member of the deal team may concede this. |
| **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN | Reject the characterisation. These terms are not settled, and nothing in our record resolves them. Our response should say Tax and IP remain open and reserved. We should not assume unlimited liability either way. |

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).** The letter makes deemed disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- This contradicts our requirement for specific fair disclosure, and we should reject it.
- Under this wording, any document anywhere in the data room or on a public register would qualify every warranty, however obscure its relevance.
- The specific disclosures in sections 2–10 are useful and should stand. Paragraph 1.2's "without limiting any specific disclosure" does not cure the general sweep.
- Require that disclosure qualifies a warranty only where the fact is **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** for a buyer to identify its nature and scope, **against the specific warranty**.

**Numbering gap.** Paragraph 1.3 is missing (the letter jumps from 1.2 to 1.4). Ask whether text was deleted or remains to be inserted. Do not accept the letter until we have the complete version.

**DL 1.4 (no admission).** "No admission" language is acceptable in principle. However, we must ensure it cannot be read to neutralise the specific disclosures. Our SPA position should treat Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and the incident as matters dealt with by conditions, completion mechanics or indemnities, not as disclosure that excuses the Seller.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records. This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion layered on constructive knowledge, which compounds the general disclosure problem.
- Delete it.
- If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry (the playbook frames the qualifier around Seller knowledge, not ours);
  - never apply to Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Completion protections

**Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3).** This customer represents about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, with change of control under cl 11.2 and conditions under cl 11.3.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
- The Disclosure Letter (s 2) confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Both elements breach our playbook. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this materiality. Consent-on-delivery risks a conditional consent that is not yet effective.
- **Require:**
  - a Completion condition of an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent;
  - documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met, delivered before Completion;
  - no Seller or Buyer waiver without our consent.

**Riverlark (cl 2 / 7).** The facility has about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change of control under cl 8.1 and discharge under cl 9.2. The Seller offers a release "following Completion". The Disclosure Letter (s 3) confirms the facility is not repaid and has no discharge.
- **Require:**
  - a current payout letter, dated near Completion and including per-diem interest;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds to Riverlark;
  - executed security releases (including PPSR and any mortgage releases) delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is not acceptable unless backed by an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** approved by Amelia Frost. Neither exists.
- Note the change-of-control clause (cl 8.1): the facility may be triggered by the sale itself, which makes repayment at Completion all the more necessary.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow).** The DD-005 closing bonuses total AUD 420,000. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. The Disclosure Letter (s 5) confirms they are not in the funds flow and are silent on on-costs.
- This is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. Once Completion occurs, these become Company obligations. If they sit outside the funds flow and outside Debt or price adjustment, we bear them economically.
- **Require** either:
  - a specific funds-flow line for AUD 420,000 **plus** triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, paid through payroll at Completion; or
  - treatment as Debt / transaction expenses deducted from price; or
  - an express Seller-funded mechanism backed by an indemnity.
- Ask for a confirmed calculation of on-costs. The Seller has not stated whether they apply.

## 4. Specific risk items

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).** The Seller says the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- The Seller itself concedes that DD-010 is not bank verification, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- We do not know whether AUD 180k is actually unpaid, or whether it is the only outstanding amount.
- **Push back:**
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have valid rights in the Ironquay Project Materials, including third-party claims and remediation or re-development cost.
  - The indemnity should not be capped at the AUD 180k figure and should sit outside the general regime.
  - Request bank evidence of payment status and an Ironquay confirmation.

**Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006).** The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material".
- That is an assertion; the Disclosure Letter (s 6) itself says access, scope and notification obligations are unestablished.
- We should equally not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure.
- **Require:**
  - preservation of all logs (download and access logs for the link, email gateway records);
  - a completed investigation, with an assessment against the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme;
  - regular written updates before Completion and prompt notice of developments;
  - Buyer consultation rights on any notification or regulator contact.
- Consider a specific indemnity outside the general regime, or a Completion condition or covenant on investigation status. Do not propose a numeric retention or price adjustment until facts are established.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller says these are ordinary-course costs. DD-008 and DD-011 show three related renewals of AUD 110k each, and the Disclosure Letter (s 8) says they must be read together and does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Neither accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor classify them automatically as Debt or a price deduction.
- Request the contracts, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment.
- Assess whether the aggregate or timing suggests pre-Completion commitment of cost outside the ordinary course (relevant to conduct-of-business covenants and working capital).
- Decide treatment after review.

**Title (DD-012).** The Seller says title is evidenced by the Company share register. The register is an internal document supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof; the Disclosure Letter (s 10) itself says it does not reflect Buyer verification.
- **Require** independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - issue and transfer history, with original share certificates or holding statements;
  - PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or rights over shares;
  - Seller board resolution and authority documents.
- Couple this with the separate Fundamental regime in Section 1.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Disclosure Letter says these involve a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not consent to a share sale. That is the Seller's characterisation.
- Have our team read the actual clauses, including any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.
- If notification is required, make it a Completion deliverable.
- These are lower-priority but should not be taken on the Seller's word.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing** in writing. Nothing in this draft is pre-cleared, and no principal-level authority is recorded on our side.
2. **Restate our liability positions:**
   - cap of 25% / AUD 6.0m;
   - de minimis AUD 5k;
   - basket AUD 50k, tipping from the first dollar;
   - 24-month general claims period.
   Do not concede the 20% cap or 18 months. Both require Amelia Frost's written approval for this draft, and we have none.
3. **Restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Insert a non-negotiable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. Delete the "all Claims of any nature" and "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" overrides.
5. **Replace general disclosure** with specific fair disclosure. Delete the data-room, public-register and constructive-knowledge sweeps, and **delete cl 8.3**. Obtain the missing DL paragraph 1.3.
6. **Bluefen:** require an effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition.
7. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and executed releases at Completion.
8. **Bonuses:** require AUD 420k plus on-costs as an express funds-flow line, as Debt, or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure and confirmatory assignment, and obtain bank evidence. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
10. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation, updates and consultation rights. Assume no conclusion either way.
11. **Sandbar:** request documents and assess before deciding treatment. No automatic Debt classification.
12. **Tax/IP:** record that these remain OPEN.
13. **Title:** require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
14. **Refresh the facts:** request a bring-down of all disclosures from 22 September 2026 to the current date, and verify the lease and Mossvale characterisations against the source documents.

**Escalation note.** If the deal team wants to consider any fallback (the 20% cap, 18 months, or a post-Completion Riverlark release), it must go to Amelia Frost for written authority identifying this draft before anything is signalled to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
